articles.title: The moment I knew: As a reality TV contestant, I was allowed one 15-minute call a week. Even at 3am, Chris would always pick up
articles.summary: Conor Curran ’s first date with Chris lasted nine hours but their relationship remained casual. Then, when Conor was at his most vulnerable, Chris was there for him. Find more stories from the moment I knew series.
body: A t 29 I had lost my career in hospitality because of Covid and decided to throw my hat in the ring as a contestant on MasterChef Australia. By the time I was eliminated in 2021, restaurants still weren’t open and I didn’t know what to do with my life. My lease was coming to an end in Melbourne and I wasn’t doing well with the lockdowns and people recognising me from TV. So I decided to retreat to my father’s place in Adelaide for a while.
By early 2022 I was dating a guy but, after a few months, he ghosted me suddenly.

One sunny autumn weekend as I was miserably assembling some flatpack furniture at Dad’s, I realised I had to get out of the house. I got on Grindr and this lovely guy, Chris, fresh from England, started messaging me.

I’d lived in the UK in my early 20s and I knew how hard it was to make friends in a new city. Still processing the shock ghosting, I invited Chris for a drink – just as mates – so neither of us had to be lonely on such a beautiful day. He said he couldn’t imagine anything better.
points: Conor Curran ’s first date with Chris lasted nine hours but their relationship remained casual.
Then, when Conor was at his most vulnerable, Chris was there for him.

articles.title: Guests Raised a Martini to Maestro Gustavo Dudamel’s Arrival at the New York Philharmonic
articles.summary: The changing of the guard at the New York Philharmonic, the oldest of America’s “Big Five” orchestras, is always a momentous occasion for the city, all the more so when the incoming music director is among the most celebrated conductors of his generation.
body: Guests were invited to don “bold black tie” attire, surely a nod to the conductor’s gift for bringing even the most stately of halls to life. That spirit—part pomp and part party, lest we forget Dudamel helped inspire the series Mozart in the Jungle —carried through the occasion.

The evening began with Venezuelan bites, including an arepa bar, on Lincoln Center’s plaza, and ended with a more traditional three-course dinner in the hall’s Grand Promenade post-performance. Rows of chairs lined the plaza’s perimeter, facing the square’s spectacular fountain. Whether intentional or not, it felt like a knowing nod to Bad Bunny’s Super Bowl shoutout to the familiar Latin family tradition of kids asleep on chairs at the function.

articles.title: My relationship with food was broken. Then I killed my own dinner
articles.summary: For years, eating was something to control, fear or regret. After I hunted my first deer, I started to see fat, hunger and my own body in a different light. I muffled my sobs with a pillow so my family couldn’t hear me from the adjacent room.
body: Pulling tear-soaked strands of hair off my cheeks, I stood in front of a full-length mirror and grabbed the fat of my thighs. If only I could just – I pictured ripping off fistfuls of my body and flinging them out the windows, where they would land on some unknowing French person six stories below. I had this vision often: pulling bits of myself off and casting them somewhere far away from me.

For years, spanning my teens and 20s, eating was either an indulgence to regret or a strategy to overplan. In high school, I chugged 32 ounces of cold green tea every morning, hoping it would burn belly fat like Instagram told me it would. While working at a deli one summer, I ate two bagel sandwiches each shift until my friend mentioned I was eating the carbohydrate equivalent of 10 slices of bread. My daily bagel intake promptly plummeted to zero. I forced myself to choke down a can of tuna in my college dorm before predawn weightlifting sessions. In my early 20s, I started experimenting with intermittent fasting: no food from 8pm until noon the next day.
points: For years, eating was something to control, fear or regret.
After I hunted my first deer, I started to see fat, hunger and my own body in a different light.

articles.title: ‘A hefty umami punch’: the best (and worst) supermarket light soy sauce, tasted and rated
articles.summary: Which salty condiment nails that deep flavour profile, and which is saltier than the sea? Our resident taster tries 10 soy sauces straight from the bottle. • The best supermarket kimchi.
body: Soy sauce was created in China about 2,200 years ago, as a means to preserve food and to zhoosh up the humble vegetarian Buddhist diet. It’s a demonstration in kokumi – literally “rich taste” – a flavour sensation that’s often called the sixth taste.

I tested all of today’s soy sauces straight from the bottle, in all their intensity. I first identified distinctive aromas such as cooked potato, sulphur and broth (all typical in soy sauce and not as off-putting as they sound), alongside caramel and malty notes. The best ones are more nuanced, with fruity high notes and vinous tones.

A delightful, wildly complex aroma with a fruity note of banana blossom and forest-floor undertones. Hits the palate with a broad flavour profile, astringent with roasted popcorn and caramel, then salt and acidity, and a strong bean base. Made from non-GMO soya beans grown in southern Taiwan, pressed only once and naturally fermented with no additives. Well worth the price.

articles.title: At the New York City Ballet Fall Fashion Gala, Stevie Nicks and Sarah Jessica Parker Brought Down the House
articles.summary: In the 14 years since Sarah Jessica Parker established the New York City Ballet’s Fall Fashion Gala, the benefit has raised more than $40 million, drawing the biggest names across the arts, fashion, and entertainment together in support of the world-renowned dance company.
body: “It’s about revisiting something that, in your mind’s eye, is extraordinary,” the multi-hyphenate and NYCB Board Vice Chair said of the occasion: a glittering night of collaboration between some of the most prominent designers and choreographers of our time. “You watch supremely talented people come together to offer New York City one of the great, great nights at the theater.”

Thursday night’s “extraordinary” affair raised $3.45 million for the company and began even before the curtain rose on a trio of world premieres: honorary gala chair Stevie Nicks made a rare red carpet appearance (her first since the Met Gala) alongside Parker. After effectively shutting down the step-and-repeat—Parker in a balletic, hand-painted custom tulle and ribbon gown by Simone Rocha, and Nicks in a mauve Morgane Le Fay frock and flower crown—the duo joined Matthew Broderick, Nicole Ari Parker, Julia Fox, and Olivia Rodrigo for the night’s performances in David H. Koch Theater.

articles.title: For Her Fashion Week Debut, Heidi Klum’s Daughter Lou Takes a Style Cue From Mom
articles.summary: Heidi Klum and daughter Lou put their own spins on the peplum for a mother-daughter moment at Vivienne Westwood.
body: It’s hardly unusual for family members to borrow from one another’s wardrobes—or, at the very least, their styling tricks. For her first Paris Fashion Week appearance, Heidi Klum’s youngest daughter, Lou, took a sartorial cue from her supermodel mom, with the pair arriving at the Vivienne Westwood spring 2027 show in coordinating peplum silhouettes and vertiginous platforms.

The matching stopped there, however. Klum stayed true to her penchant for high-impact glamour in a sculptural white blazer with sweeping, rounded lapels, its waist cinched with gold buttons before flaring into a petal-like hem. She paired it with a matching floor-skimming column skirt and inky blue stacked platform heels. Lou, meanwhile, gave the silhouette a distinctly Gen Z spin in an acid-wash pink denim top with a raw, flared waistline and asymmetric matching miniskirt, finished with a snakeskin-print shoulder bag, and floral strapped platforms.

Beauty-wise, there was another subtle echo. Both wore their hair loose—Klum’s blonde lengths tousled around her shoulders, Lou’s brunette curls left voluminous and natural—and leaned into warm, smoky makeup.
points: Heidi Klum and daughter Lou put their own spins on the peplum for a mother-daughter moment at Vivienne Westwood.
